handbookNote: Vermont Real Estate Broker license exam. Part of the 2026-09-03 R26 population-tier broker buildout (population order: UT > NV > IA > AR > KS > MS > ID > NE > WV > HI > NH > MT > RI > DE > SD > ND > AK > VT > WY -- VT is the last state built in this tier). GENUINELY UNIQUE split-vendor structure in this campaign: the National/General portion is administered by PSI Services LLC (Candidate Information Bulletin, Copyright 2025, effective 12/1/2025) -- 90 scored items (worth 100 points, some broker items score up to 2 points, the same PSI quirk seen in HI/NH/ND), 150 minutes, flat 75% pass, $110 fee. The State portion is administered DIRECTLY by the Vermont Office of Professional Regulation (OPR) itself, NOT by PSI or any exam vendor -- confirmed via an official OPR notice dated 2/19/2021: 'the Vermont State Real Estate Examination for Brokers and Salespersons will no longer be administered through an examination service. It will now be administered by the Office of Professional Regulation (OPR) as part of the initial application process... National Examination is still required and administered by PSI Services as usual.' The State portion is 50 multiple-choice/true-false items (100 points, 2 pts each), flat 75% pass, self-paced/UNTIMED (completed as part of the online license application, answer sheet uploaded -- not a timed proctored sitting). Combined: 140 items, flat 75% pass. track_registry models this as exam_question_count=140, exam_duration_sec=14400, pass_percent=75, min_correct=105 (round(140*0.75)) -- the 14400s (240min) combined duration is a self-set practice benchmark for the untimed State portion (150min real National timer + a 90min practice allowance for the State portion, consistent with this campaign's other split-portion states), not a real State-portion time limit. NATIONAL PORTION (90 items, 11 sections) reuses the exact same real PSI national item bank as Iowa/Mississippi/Hawaii/New Hampshire/North Dakota -- Vermont's own Broker outline weights are IDENTICAL (10/5/8/9/19/13/7/5/6/12/6 across the same 11 sections) -- confirmed via the official PSI bulletin's content outline. VERMONT STATE PORTION (real content, ~40 of 50 real items shared with the Salesperson version, no official per-topic item-count outline published by OPR -- unlike PSI-administered states, so this bank was organized by real statutory sub-area instead of official item counts): Commission Powers and Licensing (26 V.S.A. Chapter 41 Subchapters 001-003 -- Commission composition/powers under Sections 2251-2252, licensing/eligibility/renewal/CE under Sections 2291-2297, penalties under Section 2213 via 3 V.S.A. Section 127 ($5,000 civil/criminal max), fee ladder under Section 2255, confirmed absence of any recovery fund or surety bond), Trust and Escrow Accounts and Broker-Specific Practice (Section 2214 and Administrative Rule 4.7 -- 5-banking-day deposit deadline, $100 individual-vs-pooled-account interest threshold, interest remitted to the Vermont Housing Finance Agency, 7-year record retention; broker-in-charge vs principal-broker distinction under Rule 1.8; brokerage firm registration under Rule 2.6; the real Section 2299 temporary-licensure-on-a-broker's-death provision, capped at 1 year with no new brokerage agreements permitted; broker experience prerequisite of 2 years as a licensed salesperson including 8 separate closed transactions under Section 2292/Rule 2.5), and Agency, Disclosure, Advertising and Sign Law (Administrative Rules 4.3/4.4 -- Vermont recognizes NON-DESIGNATED and DESIGNATED agency only, with NO true dual-agency option and NO facilitator/transaction-broker status at all; a real confidentiality-wall mechanism between designated agents at the same firm whose knowledge is not imputed to each other; Rule 4.6 mandatory written consumer disclosure with a 12-month re-disclosure window; Rule 4.12 advertising rules; the genuinely distinctive 10 V.S.A. Section 493 on-premise real estate sign law under Title 10 (Conservation and Development), not Title 26 -- 6 sq ft cap on for-sale/for-lease signs, prohibited sold/pending riders, 150 sq ft/25 ft general activity sign limits, plus Section 495's general highway-sign prohibitions). Governing law: 26 V.S.A. Chapter 41 (Real Estate Brokers and Salespersons) and the Vermont Real Estate Commission Administrative Rules (effective 12/1/2015). This bank was drafted across 3 new state-topic drafting passes, each backfilled once after the initial pass landed below this project's 4:1 pool-depth floor (Vermont's real state exam is genuinely small -- only 50 real items with substantial Salesperson/Broker overlap -- so reaching the floor required deliberately deeper statute/rule mining, not padding). One real cross-file near-duplicate (the Section 2299 temporary-license 1-year duration, independently drafted in both the Commission Powers and the Trust/Escrow files) was found and removed, kept in the Trust/Escrow file as the more natural topical home. Answers were deterministically rotated into final A/B/C/D position via scripts/tracks/rotate_broker_answers.js.
